title: How To Increase Business Profitability With 7 Tips
summary: Learn how to increase business profitability by minimizing your operating expenses, reviewing financial statements, and creating healthy profit margins.
body_markdown:
Profitability is one of the strongest indicators of a company’s long-term sustainability and success. Learning how to increase business profitability lets businesses expand, develop new products, attract capital, and, most importantly, survive.


Rising fuel and shipping costs place increasing pressure on small businesses. Two-thirds of small businesses report increasing expenses and half say profit is falling, according to a June 2026 report by[Small Business Majority](https://smallbusinessmajority.org/our-research/voice-of-main-street/rising-gas-prices-and-expenses-squeeze-small-businesses) . High costs for utilities, raw materials, and employee health insurance add to the burden. Increasing sales can’t paper over rising expenses that result in weak earnings; the key is generating more profit from those sales. This article covers the difference between profitability and sales, factors that affect profitability, and approaches you can take to boost your business’s bottom line.


## What is business profitability?


Business profitability is a company’s ability to generate net income from its sales, after accounting for all direct and indirect costs, as well as taxes. It shows whether a business is successfully balancing revenue generation, cost control, and operational efficiency.


Revenue retained as earnings after deducting costs lets your company reinvest capital in business growth, be financially self-sufficient, and build cash reserves to weather downturns. Among other things, consistent profitability shows owners and investors that the company has achieved long-term cost efficiency.


Businesses typically measure profitability using[profit margins](https://www.shopify.com/blog/profitability-ratios) , which compare different types of profit to total revenue. These include:


-


**[Gross profit margin](https://www.shopify.com/blog/gross-margin-ratio) .** This is revenue minus the[cost of goods sold](https://www.shopify.com/blog/cost-of-goods-sold) for pricing purposes.


-


**[Operating margin](https://www.shopify.com/blog/operating-profit-margin)** **.** This is gross profit minus fixed costs to measure efficiency.


-


**[Net profit margin](https://www.shopify.com/blog/net-profit-margin) .** This is net income after accounting for all expenses as well as taxes, the ultimate measure of financial health.


## What’s the difference between profitability and sales?


Although both sales and profit are expressed in dollar amounts, they tell you different things about your business.


Profit shows how much of a company’s sales remain after subtracting expenses. This profit figure, also known as net income, is found at the very end of a business’s income statement, and for this reason it often is referred to as the bottom line.


Sales are the first entry on a company’s[income statement](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-income-statement) , referred to as the top line. Sales indicate only the money a company receives in exchange for selling goods and services to customers. Viewed in isolation, sales figures contain no information about potential problems, such as low margins or high operating costs.


A company could take steps to bring in much more revenue, but if its direct costs balloon simultaneously, the business’s net profit could decline or even result in losses on each item sold.


## What affects business profitability?


Business profitability has four major drivers:


-


**Price.** The amount charged per item; your product[pricing strategy](https://www.shopify.com/blog/pricing-strategies) acts as the foundation of your profitability.


-


**Sales volume.** The total amount of products or services sold; increasing your sales volume goes hand in hand with[scaling your business](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-scale-small-business) .


-


**Variable costs.**[Variable costs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-variable-cost) are expenses that fluctuate directly with production volume (like raw materials, labor costs, and shipping).


-


**Fixed costs.**[Fixed costs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-fixed-cost) are overhead that changes little, no matter your production volume (like rent and insurance).

## 7 ways to increase profitability


1. Examine your P&L to identify opportunities
2. Cut unnecessary costs
3. Increase conversion rates
4. Tweak your marketing strategy
5. Negotiate better contracts with suppliers
6. Increase customer lifetime value
7. Automate repeatable tasks


Profit maximization generally requires companies to both reduce costs and increase revenue, and ecommerce operators have several levers they can pull on both sides of the equation. Here’s how you can increase business profitability:


### 1. Examine your P&L to identify opportunities


Before making changes to your business, look at the numbers and find your biggest profit drivers, as well as any hidden drags on your profitability.


Andrew Faris, founder and CEO of ecommerce marketing agency[AJF Growth](https://ajfgrowth.com/) , says a solid understanding of the inputs into your[profit and loss statement (P&L)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/profit-and-loss-statements) is an essential part of his role as a leader.


“My job as the CEO of the brand is to go and tweak all those things until there’s a profit number on the bottom of my P&L that looks good,” he says on an[episode of Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/andrew-faris-pnl) . “And if there is no amount of tweaking that is going to make that work, then I have a broken business.”


Pull information from tools like[Shopify Finance Reports](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/default-reports/finances-report) to supplement your profit and loss statements. Scour this information closely: Assess cash flow timing. Study the costs of your production processes and compare them to earlier periods. Review individual product lines to isolate what’s actually making money.


With this baseline understanding of the data, you can find the strongest opportunities for cost reduction and sales improvement.


### 2. Cut unnecessary costs


As you review those P&L statements, investigate any costs that deviate significantly from your forecasts. This could indicate unnecessary expense creep, uncover where supplier price increases have slowly become untenable, or reveal costs that don’t justify the investment.


Consider questions like:


-


Do you still use that software subscription you bought when you started your business?


-


Is your marketing agency generating enough sales to pay for itself and then some?


-


Can you reduce labor costs by outsourcing tasks like inventory management or shipping?


-


Do you need as much office or warehouse space as you initially thought, or can you downsize or combine spaces to reduce overhead?


Line-by-line analysis of these costs can help you identify which expenses deliver a strong[return on investment](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-return-on-investment) and those that no longer justify their cost.


### 3. Increase conversion rates


One of the most effective ways to boost your company’s sales is to increase your[average conversion rate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ecommerce-conversion-rate) , which is the percentage of website visitors who take a desired action like making a purchase.[Increased conversion rates](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/how-to-increase-conversion-rate) mean more sales from the same amount of traffic.


You can[improve your website conversion](https://www.shopify.com/blog/website-conversion) rate by ensuring you have a responsive and attractive page that works on mobile devices, which a majority of customers now use to shop on ecommerce sites. Prominently display[customer testimonials](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-testimonials) and reviews as[social proof](https://www.shopify.com/blog/social-proof) , which customers often rely on for making purchase decisions.


Review[heat maps](https://www.shopify.com/blog/heat-maps) to see where customers spend time on your site, and run[A/B tests](https://www.shopify.com/blog/the-complete-guide-to-ab-testing) to determine whether certain pages, designs, or prices drive more conversions. Reduce any friction for customers in the buying journey, such as slow[site speed](https://www.shopify.com/blog/shopify-site-speed) or a complicated checkout process.


These changes may seem small, but they can make a big difference for ecommerce operators. According to data aggregated from[Plausible Analytics](https://plausible.io/blog/bounce-rate) and[Convertcart](https://www.convertcart.com/blog/ecommerce-bounce-rate) , the average ecommerce[bounce rate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/bounce-rate) , when customers leave a site without taking action, was between 36% and 47% in 2025. Reducing that rate typically boosts conversions.


### 4. Tweak your marketing strategy


Studying your[sales analytics](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sales-analytics) , such as sales performance and customer behavior, can provide insights about your most profitable customers and how they find you.


You can analyze revenue by customer segments using tools like[Shopify Profit Reports](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/shopify-reports/report-types/default-reports/profit-reports) to see what type of customer earns you the widest profit margins. Are you marketing to 30-somethings, but it’s the 50-plus set that places the highest-ticket orders? Are[affiliate](https://www.shopify.com/blog/affiliate-marketing) links worth the commissions you pay to influencers? Are you missing or underinvesting in the platforms where your[target audience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/target-audience) spends time?


Answering these questions about your most profitable customers helps you allocate your marketing budget based on which initiatives and channels result in the best return on investment. Strict adherence to that principle helped Maurice Mosseri shape marketing strategy and beyond for his fashion brand[Still Here](https://www.stillhere.nyc/) .


“All the decisions we made couldn’t just be for brand or for marketing purposes; they had to have an accountable return on investment,” Maurice says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/still-here-fashioning-success) . “So if we were spending $1,000, that had to come back as $2,000 or more.”


### 5. Negotiate better contracts with suppliers


To reduce costs, you can often negotiate more advantageous terms with vendors. Ask for multi-year agreements to lock in lower prices, shop around, conduct market research, and ask vendors if they can match a competitor’s offer. Request bundled pricing when buying multiple products or services from a supplier, which often costs less than buying items separately.


As your business grows, increased order volume can be a powerful negotiating tool. By ordering in larger quantities, the nutrition brand[IQBAR](https://www.eatiqbar.com/) reduced costs and increased earnings.


Will Nitze, the company’s founder and CEO,[says on Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/iqbar-supply-chain-and-profitability-tips) , “Go back to every one of your vendors and say, ’Hey, now that I’m buying 10 times more product, I need you to ship in trucks instead of less than a truckload, and reduce my labor \[cost\].’ You systematically go through your entire value chain and twist dials in every single spot.”


### 6. Increase customer lifetime value


Customer relationship management is critical to increasing[customer lifetime value](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-customer-lifetime-value) , or the[net profit](https://www.shopify.com/blog/net-profit-margin) your company can generate from a customer during their entire relationship with your business. The key is improving customer retention, which can boost sales and reduce costs because it’s more cost-effective to keep customers than to acquire new customers.


One effective tool is a customer[loyalty program](https://www.shopify.com/blog/loyalty-program) that encourages repeat purchases with rewards, such as special-edition products, discounts, and freebies. Deals specific to existing customers can help garner goodwill. Offer[upsells](https://www.shopify.com/blog/upselling-and-cross-selling) like bundled products for a reduced total package price. Make returns easy, and consider exceptional customer service like granting policy exceptions for your most loyal customers, such as allowing a return even though it’s a few days past your standard window.


### 7. Automate repeatable tasks


Automation using[artificial intelligence](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-ai) and other tools can improve[time management](https://www.shopify.com/blog/time-management-apps) and reduce effort, which ultimately results in lower costs. This also frees up employees to spend time contributing in higher-value ways.


Time- and labor-saving tools include[inventory management software](https://www.shopify.com/retail/inventory-management) that automatically creates replenishment orders when stock levels fall below a set threshold.[Automated emails](https://www.shopify.com/blog/57720581-7-automated-email-campaigns-that-win-customers-and-keep-them-coming-back) sent to customers after their purchase can seek feedback, prompt an upsell, or offer future discounts.[Customer service automation](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-service-automation) can help shoppers with basic tasks like order status and starting a return.


“If you can lower your G&A \[general and administrative costs\] and your payroll, you can operate much more profitably,” Matt Scanlan, founder and CEO of cashmere company[Naadam](https://naadam.co/) , says on[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/naadam-financing) .


## How to increase business profitability FAQ


### How can a business improve profitability?


Business profitability is the result of ensuring that sales of goods and services exceed the costs of delivering them to customers. To increase profitability, examine your cash flow management for opportunities, cut unnecessary costs, increase conversion rates, tweak your marketing strategy based on sales data, negotiate better contracts with suppliers, increase customer lifetime value, and automate repeatable tasks.


### How do you measure business profitability?


[Profitability ratios](https://www.shopify.com/blog/profitability-ratios) , which involve dividing various types of profit figures by total revenue, offer various measurements of business performance. These include gross profit margin for setting pricing, operating margin to measure efficiency, and net profit margin to gauge overall financial health.


### Which ecommerce metrics have the biggest impact on profit?


Several[key performance indicators (KPIs)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-kpi) affect how much profit a company earns, including total sales, direct and indirect expenses, and customer retention rate.
